rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Task selection drives outcome - name floor AND ceiling
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 20: "A bigger piece: a refactor, or a feature with unknowns... Roughly 30 to 120 minutes of the agent working" carries a soft time ceiling but no bolded anti-pattern callout (rule's example: "A task that spans a few files. Not an epic."). Line 32 goes further and names "an epic you're about to start" as an example of the repo's future work, the opposite framing from the rule's required ceiling. Rule 34 explicitly names "prework" as one of its two required placements. Harm the rule guards against: positive-only task-size criteria read as compatible with epic-sized selection, so a student picks a multi-day-scope task for the agent-sized slot, blowing the module's time budget and pedagogy. The harm is plausibly present: line 32's own wording invites exactly that reading, even though it's describing repo backlog composition rather than literally instructing epic-selection for a single exercise.
